$comment:
JSON has no comment syntax, so this human-facing note uses JSON Schema's $comment. The notebook strips it before handing the schema to the model, so nothing here reaches the LLM.

Worked example of a conforming output (a 75-word informational passage about trees):

{
  "grade_band": "4-5",
  "alternative_grade_band": "2-3",
  "scaffolding_needed": "Pre-teach the term 'photosynthesis' with a simple diagram or analogy (e.g. leaves as tiny solar-powered kitchens) before students read independently.",
  "reasoning": "1. Quantitative analysis: ~75 words across 7 sentences; FK = 0.39 * 10.7 + 11.8 * 1.4 - 15.59 = 5.1, suggesting grade 5.\n2. Qualitative complexity: TEXT STRUCTURE - Slightly Complex. LANGUAGE FEATURES - Slightly to Moderately Complex: familiar vocabulary with one technical term ('photosynthesis'). PURPOSE - Slightly Complex. KNOWLEDGE DEMANDS - Slightly Complex.\n3. Background knowledge: grade 2+ have enough knowledge of plants; 'photosynthesis' may need grade 4+ science exposure.\n4. Synthesis: grade 4-5 for independent reading; 2-3 reachable with scaffolding on the science vocabulary."
}

Note both band fields carry a SPAN of grades ('4-5'), never a single grade. Source of the example: sdks/settings/grade-level-appropriateness/contracts.toml, cases.trees.
title: EvaluatorOutput
description: Final evaluator output for the Grade Level Appropriateness evaluator.

reasoning.description: Numbered bullet points for each of the 3 analysis steps (quantitative, qualitative, background knowledge), followed by a 4th bullet point called 'synthesis'.

grade_band.description: Target grade band for the text at independent reading.

alternative_grade_band.description: A second grade band that could read and comprehend the text with the scaffolding named in scaffolding_needed, or as a read-aloud.

scaffolding_needed.description: The types of scaffolding (picture, graph, additional context, vocabulary pre-teaching, ...) that make the text accessible at alternative_grade_band.

GradeBand.description: A band on the CCSS text-complexity scale — a span of grades, not a single grade. 'CCR' is College and Career Readiness, so '11-CCR' spans grades 11-12 and the college/career-readiness benchmark rather than terminating at grade 12.
